identity.real_world_identity_notes: Caterham Seven 620R, the supercharged two-litre Ford Duratec car of 310 bhp that replaced the Superlight R500 as the most extreme Seven. It uses a six-speed sequential gearbox with flat-shift.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.

This is a different car from the curated Caterham Academy and Supersport, which are five-speed H-pattern cars. The Seven name is shared; the gearbox is not, and no controls are inherited between them.

The downshift blip is required because a racing sequential of this type engages by dogs rather than synchronisers. The reviewed source names the gearbox but not its engagement, so that is an inference; a source showing a synchronised sequential would make the blip optional.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.caterham-620r.20260814t180043110z-be2e3dd4 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the 620R and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source states a six-speed sequential gearbox with flat-shift, and the live drive selected six gears through a sequential stick with automatic cut on upshifts. Flat-shift is the manufacturer's term for that cut, so source and drive describe the same mechanism.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Supercharged 310 bhp Seven on a six-speed sequential with flat-shift, so an upshift needs neither clutch nor lift. Blip every downshift yourself. There is very little car wrapped around this drivetrain, and an unmatched downshift steps the rear out quickly.
